newsitem.title: UK: British Steel drops after ADR decline.
newsitem.headline: British Steel drops after ADR decline.

text.p: Shares in British Steel Plc dropped sharply in pre-market trade on Thursday, after a fall in the company's ADRs in the U.S. on Wednesday, dealers said.
British Steel shares were down 6-1/2p at 136 by 0706 GMT, after its ADRs fell $1-1/8 to $22-1/4.
"There was a bit of selling in the stock in the U.S. yesterday," said one market-maker, adding that he was not aware of any specific story behind the decline.

Today's decline took British Steel shares to their lowest level since July 1994. The stock has fallen steadily since the end of September, weighed down as the strength of sterling prompted a round of analyst downgrades to profit expectations.
Most recently on April 10 Morgan Stanley and Salomon Brothers cut fiscal 1998 pre-tax profit estimates to 195 million stg and 95 million respectively.
The company is due to announce its results for the year ended March 1997 on June 16.
